findings.title: iss claim accepts an array, permitting issuer spoofing via loose (any-element) match
findings.evidence: validateClaimValues at src/verifier.js:159 accepts a claim as soon as ANY element of the presented value matches: `values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v)))`. This is reached from the validator loop in verifyToken (src/verifier.js:209-227), which converts an array claim into `values = arrayValue ? value : [value]` (lines 211-212) for every claim, and the `array` argument of validateClaimType (lines 144-152, called at line 221) only changes the error message, so an array of strings still passes the `typeof v === 'string'` type check. The iss validator registered at src/verifier.js:474-476 has no single-value/array restriction (unlike aud at line 471 which sets `array: true`). Consequently a validly signed JWT whose payload contains "iss": ["https://attacker.example", "https://trusted-issuer"] passes the allowedIss check because the trusted issuer is just one matching element, even though RFC 7519 requires iss to be a single StringOrURI. An attacker who can obtain a token signed by a key the application trusts (shared/multi-issuer keys, or verifiers such as get-jwks that do not independently validate iss) can place their own issuer first in the array alongside the legitimate one and have the token accepted, spoofing the issuer and bypassing allowedIss-based trust decisions (CVE-2025-30144 / GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8); upstream fixed this by replacing the line with `values.every(...)` in 5.0.6.
